title: Introduction: 40,000 Support Tickets and SQL Limits
text: Hi, I am Hussein and this video is about Snowflake Cortex running AI inside your database. 40,000 support tickets sit in a Snowflake table. SQL can count them. It cannot read them, so I asked Claude where to start. Here is the whole idea. Cortex is not another platform to integrate. It is a SQL function you already know how to call. The model comes to the data, not the other way around. Your warehouse is excellent at the structured columns, ticket ID, timestamp

title: The Model Comes to the Data: Cortex vs External Pipelines - Ticket Triage in SQL: Classify, Sentiment, and Summarize
text: Region. It is blind to the one that matters, the body. Counting rows is easy. Knowing which ones are angry about billing is not. The usual answer is a pipeline. Export the text, send it to a model API, load the answers back, a second system, a second copy of your data. Cortex inverts it. The model runs inside Snowflake and your grants still apply. So, the starter use case is small enough to finish, ticket triage. Watch how ordinary the query looks. That is the whole thing, three Cortex functions in a select list. Classify text picks from a label set you define. Sentiment scores -1 to +1. Summarize writes the one-liner. No infrastructure anywhere. The output is just a table. Same warehouse, same grants, three new columns you can group by. Billing complaints sorted by how angry they are. That is a dashboard query now. Now, where it bites.
